notes:
CIRCUIT: a large multi-stage discrete transistor network (9 BJTs, 6 resistors, 2 diodes, 5 single-port supply arrows +15V/+10V/+6V/+5V/+3V, 1 GND). A +15V rail across the top feeds a 15k-15k divider on the left (tapped at +10V) and the collector of Q3 on the right. Mid-sheet a 150ohm and a 15k resistor form a horizontal chain at y~360 tapped at +6V. A two-diode string (D5, D11) runs vertically at x~695. The bottom rail at y~840 is ground. 23 components, 16 nets.

JUDGEMENT CALLS (sites):
  - S18 (695,368) + S19 (709,373), both CRITICAL, tracer default junction, hop reported 0.0: OVERRIDDEN TO A CROSSING via explicit edge groups. At 14x zoom the x~695 vertical (the diode string between D#5's cathode and D#11's anode) clearly makes a smooth S-shaped SIDEWAYS JOG: it bends right to x~709, passes the y~370 horizontal, and bends back left to x~695. The horizontal (right end of R#8 heading east to the +5V node) runs straight through the middle of that jog. Per the sheet's own convention this is the 'not connected' gesture. The tracer's hop detector missed it only because the single drawn jog got skeletonised into TWO sites 14px apart, so neither site saw a complete arc. DRAFTER'S HABIT (decisive): site S52 (576,760) is the very same gesture - vertical jogs right around a horizontal - and there the tracer DID measure hop=13.2 and defaulted to crossing. Two identical gestures must read the same way. Expressed as sites.18 = [[37,46,49],[45,47]] and sites.19 = 'none': e37 (D5 cathode down to y=365) + e46 (the arc crown) + e49 (the arc down to D11's anode) form the vertical group; e45 (R#8 right end, x 575->692) + e47 (x 711->826, to the +5V node) form the horizontal group. Consequence of the other reading (junction): D#5's cathode, D#11's anode, R#8's right end and the whole +5V column would collapse into ONE 7-terminal net, shorting out the diode string's midpoint and destroying the series-diode structure; net n6 would disappear entirely.
  - S52 (576,760) CRITICAL, tracer default crossing: CONFIRMED CROSSING. 14x zoom shows the same S-jog - the R#16 column comes down at x~564, bows right to x~578, passes the y~760 horizontal and returns to x~560 before continuing to the bottom rail. Junction here would tie R#16's bottom (which is ground) to Q#12's collector / Q#17's collector / Q#20's base, shorting that whole signal node to ground and leaving Q#20 with a grounded base - electrically dead. Crossing it is.
  - S29 (829,388) deg=4 CRITICAL, dot=2.5, hop=3.6: JUNCTION. inkmap at (829,388) shows the crossing region swelling to roughly 12px wide x 6px tall against a 4px vertical stroke and a 3px horizontal stroke - a symmetric blob fatter than either stroke in BOTH axes, i.e. a solder dot, and it is the fattest site on the sheet along with S26/S58. Crucially there is NO jog here, and this drafter jogs whenever they mean 'not connected' (S18/S19, S52). Consequence of crossing: the +5V arrow and R#8's right end would form one 2-terminal net while Q#3's emitter, Q#15's emitter and Q#21's collector formed another - possible but it contradicts both the blob and the drafter's demonstrated convention.
  - S16 (440,358) deg=4 CRITICAL, dot=2.1, hop=3.6: JUNCTION. inkmap shows a solid ~8x9 px blob against 3px strokes - a genuine solder dot. It ties the 150ohm/15k midpoint, the +6V arrow and Q#12's emitter together. Crossing would strand the +6V arrow with only Q#12's emitter and split the resistor chain, leaving R#8's left end connected to nothing but Q#12 - and there is no jog.
  - S8 (256,248), S17 (260,362), S36 (824,503), S38 (55,554), S39 (693,569), S53 (155,832), S54 (244,836), S55 (436,842), S56 (547,850), S58 (686,864) - all CRITICAL, all JUNCTION. Each crop shows a clean T (a lead terminating on a through-running wire), not a 4-way crossing, so 'crossing' is not even expressible; the only alternative, 'none', would float a lead. S58 additionally carries a heavy blob (dot=2.5). Recorded explicitly to document that each was inspected.
  - Non-critical sites S0-S7, S9-S15, S20-S28, S30-S35, S37, S40-S50, S57 were all inspected in the montages and are self-intersections of handwritten labels ('+15V', '+10V', '+6V', '+5V', '+3V', '15 kohm', '150 ohm', '50 kohm') or symbol ink (resistor zigzags, transistor lead corners, the GND hatch). None touch a component terminal, so they were left at their defaults.

PORT FIXES:
  - VDC#0 (+15V), VDC#6 (+6V), VDC#7 (+5V): each t0 was bound to a stroke of its own handwritten '+NNV' caption instead of the arrow's foot, producing three 1-terminal nets. Re-bound to the arrow feet: #0 -> p3 (525,141) on the top rail at S4, #6 -> p1 (443,341) on the y~358 chain at S16, #7 -> p1 (943,380) on the y~386 wire at S27. VDC#2 (+10V) and VDC#13 (+3V) were already on their feet and were left alone.
  - PIN ORDER, all four BJT-PNPs (#10, #12, #14, #15): the tracer assumed emitter = bottom lead on every transistor. On this sheet all four PNPs are drawn with the EMITTER on the UPPER lead. Verified at 9x on each: the arrowhead sits on the upper lead with its barbs opening away from the base bar and its point landing ON the base bar, i.e. the arrow points INTO the base, which is the PNP emitter convention; the lower lead is plain. Applied (collector, base, emitter): #10 -> (p1 bottom, p2 left, p0 top); #12 -> (p0 bottom, p2 right, p1 top); #14 -> (p0 bottom, p1 left, p2 top); #15 -> (p0 bottom, p1 left, p2 top).
  - All five BJT-NPNs (#3, #17, #18, #20, #21) were checked at 9x and are already correct: arrowhead on the LOWER lead pointing AWAY from the base bar (NPN emitter), so (collector, base, emitter) = (top, side, bottom) as the tracer had it. No change.

CLASSES: all 23 symbols match their labels. The four PNPs and five NPNs are distinguishable by arrow direction as described above and agree with the COCO classes. Diodes #5 and #11 are both drawn triangle-down with the bar below (anode up, cathode down). No re-classification needed.

UNRESOLVED / NOTED: (a) net n15 is a bare base-to-base tie between Q#17 and Q#18 with no third connection - unusual but that is what is drawn; I re-traced the entire y~664 run at 3x and nothing else touches it. (b) net n6, the D#5/D#11 midpoint, is likewise a 2-terminal net; it is a consequence of the S18/S19 crossing above and is exactly what a series diode string with an unloaded midpoint looks like. (c) All 40 gap bridges were reported as netlist-neutral and were left alone. ERC clean: 23 components, 16 nets, every terminal assigned.
